title: Public Algorithm Transparency Register Pattern
description: A pattern for maintaining a public, proactively-updated register of every algorithm a public body uses in eligibility or administrative decisions, including its logic and the criteria it applies, published before any disclosure dispute arises.
problem: Public bodies deploy administrative algorithms and only face pressure to explain their logic after a disclosure request or legal challenge, by which point applicants may already have been wrongly denied for years with no visibility into why.
solution: Maintain a public register listing every algorithm used in an eligibility or administrative decision, its intended purpose, its decision logic in plain language, and a channel for civil-society review — published proactively as a matter of course, not produced defensively in response to a request.
applicability: Any public body deploying an algorithm to determine eligibility for a benefit, service, or other administrative outcome.
consequences: Publishing decision logic can expose it to gaming by applicants seeking to satisfy criteria without genuinely qualifying; maintaining an accurate, current register requires an ongoing documentation discipline that can lapse without dedicated ownership.

citations.title: Civio pulls back the curtain on public algorithms — Spain's Supreme Court orders the Government to release BOSCO's source code

relationships.reason: A public register is a concrete mechanism satisfying this control's transparency requirement.
The pattern's output is a public algorithm documentation publication record.
